name: Nemrut Dağ
description: On a 2,150-metre summit in the Taurus Mountains of southeastern Türkiye, King Antiochus I of Commagene built a hilltop tomb-sanctuary in the 1st century BC. Colossal stone statues of gods and the king himself sit on terraces beside a huge mound of stones. Their blend of Greek and Persian traditions reflects the kingdom's mixed heritage, and the site is especially popular at sunrise.
